subject: MgmtLink upgrade caused intermittent VPC controlpath timeouts — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Amira Khan <amira@healthscout.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthScout Platform Ops <infra+ops@healthscout.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent VPC controlpath timeouts after MgmtLink upgrade

Hi Rishi —

We started seeing intermittent controlpath timeouts to our private deployment after you rolled the MgmtLink 2.1.0 upgrade across our VPC at ~08:40 PDT. The agent nodes stay up but the control channel (management link) reports repeated timeouts and some API calls are failing (500/502) to our app. This has led to ~2 minutes of increased latency and a couple of failed inference requests per minute.

I've attached a small set of logs we captured. Can you confirm whether the upgrade had a config change that might affect keepalive/heartbeat behavior? We are in US-West and currently in prod.

Thanks,
Amira
Platform SRE — HealthScout
[attachment: healthscout-ctrlpath-sample-20270415.log (text/plain)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Khan <amira@healthscout.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPC controlpath timeouts after MgmtLink upgrade

Thanks Amira — we see the alerts on our side as well.

Short answer: we pushed MgmtLink 2.1.0 at 08:30 PDT which included a change to the controlplane keepalive backoff (intended to reduce noisy reconnects). In limited internal validation that change looked fine, but it can extend the period before a stale connection is cleaned up in certain NAT+FW environments.

Immediate next steps from Redwood: 
- I've escalated to our infra on-call (cc'd Grace & Dev).
- We'll collect full controlpath traces and the agent-side heartbeat dumps.
- If required, we can roll the MgmtLink config back for HealthScout or push a targeted fix.

Can you share the exact NAT/firewall device or cloud egress behavior in your VPC? That will help us reproduce.

Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Amira Khan <amira@healthscout.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPC controlpath timeouts after MgmtLink upgrade

Amira — thanks for the logs. I pulled the agent heartbeat window and we can see a pattern: after the upgrade the agent increased the controlplane keepalive interval from 15s -> 45s when experiencing transient EGRESS resets. On HealthScout's network that extended interval allowed a staggered cluster of connections to be marked alive longer, which worsened queue build-up on the controlplane side and produced timeouts under bursty workloads.

Plan: 
1) Short term mitigation: push a config patch to set keepalive to 20s (safe) and reduce backoff. We can push this as a non-disruptive config update to the deployed agents in the next 30 minutes.
2) If the mitigation doesn't restore steady state, we will schedule a targeted rollback of the MgmtLink change only for your VPC.
3) We'll capture end-to-end traces and provide an RCA writeup by Tuesday.

We will attach the action log and the proposed config diff.

Grace
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: mgmtlink-upgrade-diff.txt (text/plain)]
From: Amira Khan <amira@healthscout.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPC controlpath timeouts after MgmtLink upgrade

Grace/Rishi — thanks, we can accept the 20s keepalive patch. HealthScout's egress uses a managed firewall with idle connection timeout of 60s and we do occasional NAT gateway churn during deployments. We'll stand by for the patch and will run a short load window to validate.

Also please send the expected change window and any risk notes we should communicate to our App team.

— Amira
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Khan <amira@healthscout.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T10:51:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPC controlpath timeouts after MgmtLink upgrade

Amira — patch pushed at 11:05 PDT to the agent fleet in your VPC: keepalive=20s, backoff steps trimmed. We applied the change to one AZ first (~10% of agents) and ramped to 100% after 3 successful minutes.

Monitoring summary (11:05–11:45 PDT): controlpath error rate dropped from 6.3 errors/min -> 0.4 errors/min. Latency spikes returned to baseline within 8 minutes of the ramp. We did observe two short 502s during the ramp that matched NAT churn events on your side.

Attachments: controlpath trace bundle and a short action plan PDF.

Dev
Software Engineer, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary and requested artifacts — MgmtLink upgrade (2027-04-15)

Amira — following up with the RCA and next steps per our agreement. Apologies again for the impact during your morning window on 2027-04-15. Below is a condensed summary and links to artifacts. Full RCA attached in Drive.

Summary: 
- Impact: intermittent controlpath timeouts and elevated inference error rates between 08:40–11:10 PDT on 2027-04-15 for HealthScout's VPC. Peak: ~2 minutes of elevated latency, 6.3 errors/min pre-mitigation.
- Root cause: a keepalive/backoff behavior introduced in MgmtLink 2.1.0 that increased keepalive interval under certain egress reset patterns. On HealthScout's NAT+firewall profile this allowed longer-lived but fragile connections which caused queueing on the controlplane and produced transient timeouts under burst traffic.
- Immediate remediation: pushed keepalive=20s patch to your agent fleet (non-disruptive) — issue resolved to baseline within ~8 minutes after full ramp.

Action items and commitments: 
1) Configuration hardening: we will ship MgmtLink 2.1.1 that restores the original keepalive/backoff defaults but keeps other 2.1.0 improvements. ETA: 2027-04-23.
2) HealthScout runbook update: we will deliver a one-page runbook for your on-call to tune NAT/idle timeouts and to detect controlpath drift. ETA: 2027-04-22.
3) Post-deploy test: a lightweight healthcheck traffic hammer will be run during future MgmtLink upgrades to detect the regressions earlier. We'll coordinate a maintenance window with you.
4) Credits: as discussed with your procurement team, we will issue a service credit for the incident window. Redwood billing will follow up.

Artifacts: runbook and full trace bundle are available at the link below. Please let us know any additional evidence you need for your auditors.

Runbook & RCA: https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/HealthScout/incident-20270415/runbook.md
Jira: INF-7421

Thanks for the fast collaboration and for verifying the patch. If you'd like a short postmortem call, I can bring Grace and Dev.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
